description: 1 staging, 2 main, 3 upper. The same rules apply on every level; a level differs only in its column values.
The control point the device belongs to (the ADR-005 name, or CP and the lowest switch number until the owner names it). Empty for a line device.
The kind of JMRI bean: turnout, fb (turnout feedback sensor), block, occupancy (a block's detector), mast, head (signal head) or sensor (a panel status lamp).

What the device is: turnout, lcc_alias, fb, os (the block through a switch's points), xover_corner, track, spur, loop_half, helix, home (a mast at a switch), intermediate (a mast between two blocks), hidden (a routing mast the panel does not show), head, spare (a detector with no block), panel_status or part (a piece of track inside another block, part_of). Readers test it, never a name prefix.
The public name under ADR-005, which is also the JMRI user name.

How the device is in JMRI now: field (the physical device is in JMRI, so jmri_name is system_name), virtual (an internal stand-in; system_name, when set, is the planned device), none (this row gives no JMRI name) or spare (a field detector with no block).
The physical or planned device (M2T408, M2S1300, IH3332), or the JMRI name of a staging mast or head. Empty when nothing is planned. A draft while assignment is virtual.

The name JMRI and the panels bind the device by. Equal to system_name when assignment is field, except a staging turnout the tables bind by its user name. For a virtual device it follows hartlib.level_devices.
The LCOS node number (the RF24 address) of the field or planned device.
A turnout's DCC address (an LCC alias carries its own). A field turnout's JMRI comment takes it as its second group (hartlib.names.jmri_comment); nothing parses it back out of a comment.
The node, port and output text of a device (Node: 4 Turnout: 0 | OU: 1 Ports: 1,2), without the DCC group. Empty when the row has a jmri_comment.
The JMRI comment of a device whose comment is not wiring text (a block's description, a mast's control point and switch, a build note). Empty when the row has wiring.
The link from the row to the drawing: the switch or track name the trial drawing used.
Text for people from the old device map: what the row is for, or why a device has no detector.
Occupancy rows: the blocks the detector serves, separated by a semicolon.
Occupancy rows: wired, planned, not_wired or none, whether the detector is in the field, planned on a node input, planned with no input yet, or not planned.
Block rows: yes when the block is a Dispatcher System station (the stop its JMRI comment carries).

Block rows of staging: the system name (ILB...) of the block's JMRI layout block, which JMRI numbered when the block was drawn. Empty on the main and upper levels, whose layout blocks the Layout Editor build numbers.

Block rows: the block this row is a piece of, when the row is a piece of track inside another block (owner, 2026-11-20: a short piece between two switches is part of the lower-numbered switch's OS block, or the block block_exceptions.csv gives it). A row with part_of has role part and assignment none: it makes no JMRI block, layout block or occupancy row of its own, and every reader of block rows skips it (hartlib.devices.OUT_OF_MAPS). The block it names exists and has no part_of itself.
Mast rows: the switch whose leg the mast stands at. Empty for an intermediate, anchor or buffer-stop mast.
Mast rows: the block the mast faces.
Mast rows: the blocks the mast protects, separated by a semicolon.
Mast rows: the way the mast looks, east or west.

The script that writes the row (build_staging_masts.py, build_device_map.py, build_main_upper_masts.py or panel_items.json). A writer rewrites only rows that carry its name and stops on any other. Empty means the owner keeps the row by hand. The allowed names are one constant in hartlib.devices.
One plain sentence saying what the device is.

The row's place in the name map, the rows (in this order) that carry the hardware ID, DCC address, control point and wiring comment below. Empty when the row has none. The name map was the file public_name_map.csv until R9e (ADR-029), and the five columns after this one hold what it carried.
The control point the name map gives the row.
The hardware the name map gives the row (a device, or a block's old detector name).
The DCC address the name map gives the row.
The wiring comment the name map gives the row.
The notes the name map gives the row.
